---
name: mrscraper-fetch
description: |
  Retrieve a known public URL with MrScraper MCP as HTML, Markdown, a screenshot, brand data, or structured JSON. Use for reading, summarizing, archiving, or extracting a page; supports browser rendering, page and proxy countries, selector waits, and retry limits. Use mrscraper-serp when no URL is known.
---

# Retrieve Page Content with MrScraper MCP

Use the MrScraper MCP tool that matches the requested representation whenever
the user already has a public URL. Keep using the retrieved content for
summarization, comparison, transformation, and structured output. Use
[mrscraper](../mrscraper/SKILL.md) for connection and authentication checks,
account status, or broader routing, and
[mrscraper-serp](../mrscraper-serp/SKILL.md) when discovery must happen first.

Use these tools only for content the user is authorized to access and in
accordance with the site's requirements. Browser rendering loads a page; it
does not click controls, submit forms, or provide an authenticated interactive
browser session.

## Step 1 — Define the Outcome

Confirm the target URL and what the user wants:

- Read, summarize, cite, or inspect the page.
- Check whether specific text appears.
- Archive the page or capture a screenshot.
- Produce fields, JSON, tables, or other structured output.
- Get the site's brand colors, typography, logos, and social links.
- Load JavaScript-rendered or country-specific content.

When many pages share a layout, retrieve representative pages, define one local
extractor, retrieve the remaining pages in parallel when safe and proportional,
and apply the same extractor to every saved response.

## Step 2 — Choose the Tool

| Tool | Description | data in the response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| scrapeHtml | Retrieve the raw HTML of a page. Browser rendering is optional. | HTML text. |
| scrapeMarkdown | Retrieve a page as Markdown. Including HTML also enables browser rendering and returns both outputs as JSON. | Markdown text; with html set to true, an object with html and markdown. |
| getScreenshot | Capture a base64 screenshot of the full page or top viewport. Browser rendering is always enabled. | An object with screenshot and the requested html and markdown. |
| scrapeJson | Extract structured JSON from a page using a natural-language prompt. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. | The extracted data in data.data, with run metadata. |
| scrapeBrand | Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links as JSON. | The brand in data.data.brand. |

The client may namespace the tool names; select the tool from the MrScraper MCP
provider. Start with the URL alone and add only the inputs the outcome needs.

scrapeMarkdown for readable text:

    {
      "url": "https://example.com"
    }

scrapeHtml rendered in a browser, waiting for an element:

    {
      "url": "https://example.com",
      "browserRendering": true,
      "waitForSelector": "body"
    }

scrapeMarkdown with the page HTML as well:

    {
      "url": "https://example.com",
      "html": true
    }

getScreenshot of the top viewport, with Markdown instead of HTML:

    {
      "url": "https://example.com",
      "screenshot": "top",
      "html": false,
      "markdown": true
    }

A screenshot is base64 image data that can be large. Request it only when the
user needs an image, and save it to a file rather than reading it into the
conversation.

scrapeJson with a prompt; append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the
output:

    {
      "url": "https://example.com",
      "prompt": "Extract the first 2 items with title and price. Json Schema: {\"type\":\"array\",\"items\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"title\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"price\":{\"type\":\"string\"}},\"required\":[\"title\",\"price\"]}}"
    }

The prompt describes the data to extract from the loaded page; it does not
navigate, click, or sign in. Without a prompt, scrapeJson extracts all data as
completely as possible. Long prompts are sent in a request body automatically.

scrapeBrand takes only the URL:

    {
      "url": "https://mrscraper.com"
    }

scrapeBrand waits up to 120 seconds. HTTP 422 with a settled job means the page
has no usable brand data.

## Step 3 — Choose Page-Loading Options

scrapeHtml, scrapeMarkdown, getScreenshot, and scrapeJson share the page
inputs. scrapeBrand accepts only url.

| MCP input | Tools | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| url | All | Required | Absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to process. |
| timeout | HTML, Markdown, screenshot, JSON | 300 | Page load timeout in seconds, from 1 to 300. The HTTP request allows 30 additional seconds. |
| geoCode | HTML, Markdown, screenshot, JSON | "us" | Two-letter country code to load the page from, sent in lowercase. |
| proxyCountry | HTML, Markdown, screenshot, JSON | "us" | Two-letter country code of the proxy server, sent in lowercase. |
| super | HTML, Markdown, screenshot, JSON | false | Whether to route the request through real devices. |
| waitUntil | HTML, Markdown, screenshot, JSON | "domcontentloaded" | Navigation completion event to wait for: domcontentloaded, load, networkidle0, or networkidle2. |
| proxy | HTML, Markdown, screenshot, JSON | Omitted | Custom proxy URL used to load the page. |
| maxRetries | HTML, Markdown, screenshot, JSON | Omitted | Maximum number of retries, as a nonnegative integer. Omit this parameter for no limit. |
| saveResult | HTML, Markdown, screenshot, JSON | false | Whether to save the result to the dashboard Result tab. |
| blockResources | HTML, Markdown, screenshot | false | Whether to block images, fonts, and stylesheets while loading the page. |
| waitForSelector | HTML, Markdown, screenshot | Omitted | Wait for the page to contain the specified CSS selector before returning the result. |
| returnCookie | HTML, Markdown, screenshot | false | Whether to include browser session cookies in the response. |
| browserRendering | HTML, Markdown, JSON | false | Whether to render the page in a browser before returning the result. |
| warmStart | HTML, Markdown | false | Whether to enable warm start for more reliable scraping, at the cost of additional latency. |
| html | Markdown, JSON | false | Whether to include the page HTML in the response. |
| html | Screenshot | true | Whether to include the page HTML in the response. |
| markdown | Screenshot | false | Whether to include the page Markdown in the response. |
| screenshot | Screenshot | "full" | Screenshot area to capture: full for the entire page or top for the top viewport. |
| screenshot | JSON | false | Whether to include a base64 screenshot in the response. |
| prompt | JSON | "Extract all data as complete as possible." | Instructions describing the data to extract. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. |

In the Tools column, HTML is scrapeHtml, Markdown is scrapeMarkdown, screenshot
is getScreenshot, and JSON is scrapeJson.

Authentication is handled by the MCP client's OAuth 2.1 connection and is
never a tool input.

## Step 4 — Inspect and Retry Deliberately

Prefer structuredContent. Check isError, error, status_code, and
headers["x-status-code"] (the target page's status) before using data. If the
response fails, is blocked, incomplete, or missing dynamic content:

1. Inspect status_code, error, headers["x-status-code"], and the content.
2. Change one input at a time: set browserRendering, wait for a later
   waitUntil event, or add waitForSelector for content that loads late.
3. Set geoCode or proxyCountry only when evidence shows that the page differs
   by country. Set super or warmStart when routing or a cold start may be the
   problem.
4. Stop after a usable response unless the user requests a comparison.

Do not repeat an identical request. Treat waitForSelector as a CSS selector,
not a duration. Omitting maxRetries means no retry limit; set a small number
when the user wants to bound retries.

## Step 5 — Deliver the Result

Answer the user's request from data. Keep the full envelope when headers or
diagnostics matter. When the user requests an archive, save the successful
response or the requested field with the environment's local file-writing
capability; the tools have no output-path input.

Keep retrieved content as the source of truth for later steps. Build
summaries, tables, JSON transformations, and extraction scripts from it, and
retrieve the page again when a follow-up needs details that an earlier
transformation did not preserve.

name: mrscraper-serp
description: |
  Discover public pages through web search with MrScraper's webSearch tool. Use when no target URL is known or the user asks to inspect web search results. After discovery, retrieve selected pages with mrscraper-fetch.
---

# Discover Pages with MrScraper MCP Web Search

Use the webSearch tool supplied by the MrScraper MCP server when a task begins
with a search query rather than a known target URL. webSearch: Search the web
and return ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources. Use
[mrscraper](../mrscraper/SKILL.md) for connection troubleshooting, account
status, or broader routing.

## Step 1 — Build the Query

Pass the query text in query. Include the important entity, attribute,
location, or date:

    {
      "query": "web scraping best practices"
    }

## Step 2 — Set the Country and Result Count

Set country to a two-letter country code when results must come from one
country. It defaults to us:

    {
      "query": "running shoes",
      "country": "id"
    }

The search returns 10 results by default. Ask for more, up to 100, only when
the user needs broader coverage:

    {
      "query": "site:example.com documentation",
      "country": "id",
      "numResults": 20
    }

### Parameters

| MCP input | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| query | Required | Search query text, trimmed before sending, containing 1 to 1000 characters. |
| country | "us" | Two-letter country code to search from, sent in lowercase. |
| numResults | 10 | Number of search results to request, as an integer from 10 to 100. Fewer results may be returned. |

A search waits up to 120 seconds. Authentication is handled by the MCP client's
OAuth 2.1 connection and is never a tool input.

## Step 3 — Inspect the Results

The complete response envelope is available in MCP structuredContent and as
formatted JSON text. Prefer structuredContent. Check isError, error, and
status_code before using data. The results are a ranked list in data.data;
each result has rank, title, url, description, and source.

When the user requests a search artifact, save the successful data or full
envelope with local file-writing capability; webSearch has no output-path
input.

## Step 4 — Continue with Relevant URLs

Select only URLs relevant to the user's goal, then load
[mrscraper-fetch](../mrscraper-fetch/SKILL.md) to retrieve and inspect each
selected page before deriving answers, comparisons, or structured output.

Run independent follow-up URLs in parallel when the environment supports safe
parallel execution. Keep the number of pages proportional to the requested
coverage. If the user only requested URL discovery, stop after the search.

## Step 5 — Handle Weak or Missing Results

- Set country when the results come from the wrong country.
- Rewrite noisy queries around the important entity, attribute, and location.
- Raise numResults only after checking the first results.
- Use [mrscraper](../mrscraper/SKILL.md) when the connection or authentication
  fails.

---
name: mrscraper
description: |
  Connect, authenticate, route, and troubleshoot MrScraper MCP, and check account usage with the status tool. For a known public URL, retrieve HTML, Markdown, a screenshot, brand data, or structured JSON with mrscraper-fetch; use mrscraper-serp for query-first discovery through web search.
---

# MrScraper MCP

Use this skill for connection and authentication checks, tool selection, shared
response handling, account status, and troubleshooting. Load the focused fetch
or SERP skill for page retrieval and web search.

MrScraper MCP has six scraping and search tools, plus account status:

| Tool | Description |
| --- | --- |
| status | Return the raw account status API response without summarizing, redacting body fields, or adding calculated fields. |
| scrapeHtml | Retrieve the raw HTML of a page. Browser rendering is optional. |
| scrapeMarkdown | Retrieve a page as Markdown. Including HTML also enables browser rendering and returns both outputs as JSON. |
| getScreenshot | Capture a base64 screenshot of the full page or top viewport. Browser rendering is always enabled. |
| scrapeBrand | Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links as JSON. |
| scrapeJson | Extract structured JSON from a page using a natural-language prompt. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. |
| webSearch | Search the web and return ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources. |

## Step 1 — Verify or Connect MrScraper MCP

Check whether the current client exposes these seven tools from the MrScraper
MCP provider:

    status  scrapeHtml  scrapeMarkdown  getScreenshot  scrapeBrand  scrapeJson  webSearch

The client may display server-qualified names. Match the provider and
unqualified tool name; do not assume a fixed namespace.

If the tools are already available, use the existing connection. If they are
missing, ask the user to enable the existing MrScraper connection or configure
the managed Streamable HTTP endpoint:

    https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp

A self-managed deployment may expose the same tools over Streamable HTTP or
stdio. Connection setup belongs to the MCP client. After setup or reconnection,
list the available tools and confirm all seven names before claiming the
integration is ready. A client that still lists scraperAPI has cached the
previous tool list; start a new session or reconnect so it loads the current
tools.

## Step 2 — Authenticate

MrScraper MCP authenticates through OAuth 2.1. Authentication belongs to the
MCP connection and is never a tool argument.

When the connection is not authorized, start the MCP client's authorization
flow. Let the client discover the authorization metadata, open the MrScraper
consent page, complete authorization, store the resulting credentials, and
refresh access tokens. The user may need to approve access in a browser, but
must not paste an authorization code, access token, refresh token, API key, or
other credential into the conversation.

Never place credentials in tool arguments, print them, write them into project
artifacts, or manually reproduce the OAuth exchange. Do not configure an
API-key or bearer-token fallback from these skills.

The connection uses two scopes: scrape:read for the six scraping and search
tools, and account:read for status. A tool called without its scope returns
403 insufficient_scope; reauthorize the connection so the client requests it.

Verify end-to-end access with status, which reads the account without
retrieving a page:

    {}

A successful response confirms that the connection can authenticate and reach
MrScraper. If it fails, report the error and do not claim setup is complete.

## Step 3 — Route the Request

| User outcome | MCP tool or skill |
| --- | --- |
| Read, summarize, or preserve a known public page | [mrscraper-fetch](../mrscraper-fetch/SKILL.md) with scrapeMarkdown, or scrapeHtml when the page structure matters |
| Capture what a page looks like | [mrscraper-fetch](../mrscraper-fetch/SKILL.md) with getScreenshot |
| Extract specific fields from a page as JSON | [mrscraper-fetch](../mrscraper-fetch/SKILL.md) with scrapeJson, or local extraction from retrieved content |
| Get a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links | [mrscraper-fetch](../mrscraper-fetch/SKILL.md) with scrapeBrand |
| Discover relevant pages from a web search query | [mrscraper-serp](../mrscraper-serp/SKILL.md) with webSearch, then retrieve selected pages |
| Check the plan, token usage, or remaining tokens | status |

### Retrieve first, extract locally

scrapeHtml and scrapeMarkdown return raw page content. Produce summaries,
tables, JSON, and other structured output from that content with local analysis
or extraction logic. The raw response preserves complete page context for later
questions, validation, and changes to the requested schema.

Use scrapeJson when the user asks MrScraper to extract the data, or when a
prompt-driven extraction is clearly simpler than local logic. Keep the raw page
as well when later questions may need details that the extraction leaves out.

Prefer this workflow for pages with a shared layout:

1. Retrieve representative pages and inspect their content.
2. Understand the shared page structure and required fields.
3. Define a stable output schema and reusable local extractor.
4. Retrieve the remaining pages, in parallel when safe.
5. Apply the same extractor to every saved response.

Request Markdown when readable text is enough and HTML when an extractor needs
the page structure.

For discovery-first work, call webSearch, select relevant URLs, and retrieve
the pages whose content will inform the answer.

MrScraper MCP does not create AI scrapers, rerun saved scrapers, or list stored
results. Point the user to the MrScraper dashboard at https://app.mrscraper.com
for those.

## Step 4 — Handle Output and Artifacts

Every tool returns the same response envelope in MCP structuredContent and in a
formatted JSON text block:

    {
      "status_code": 200,
      "data": {},
      "headers": {}
    }

data holds the API response body: HTML or Markdown text from scrapeHtml and
scrapeMarkdown, and JSON from the other tools. Prefer structuredContent when
available. An HTTP or network failure adds error and sets the MCP result's
isError flag; a network failure has status_code null. Invalid inputs are
rejected before any request is sent. Check those signals before trusting data.
Credential-bearing response headers are removed.

MrScraper tools do not accept output paths. When the user requests an artifact,
wait for a successful tool result, select the requested value, and save it with
the environment's local file-writing capability. A screenshot is base64 image
data in data.screenshot; decode it before saving an image.

Save substantial intermediate artifacts under the current project's
.mrscraper directory unless the user specifies another location. This project
artifact directory is unrelated to MCP connection credentials. Keep artifacts
out of version control unless the user asks to commit them.

saveResult defaults to false. Set it to true only when the user wants a
scraping result kept in the MrScraper dashboard Result tab.

## Step 5 — Review Account Usage

Call status with an empty object:

    {}

data is the raw account status response, without summaries or calculated
fields. Account details are in data.data, including tokenLimit, tokenUsage,
subscriptionItem, and scraperAllowance:

    {
      "status_code": 200,
      "data": {
        "message": "...",
        "data": {
          "tokenLimit": 100000,
          "tokenUsage": 2500,
          "stripeStatus": "active",
          "subscriptionItem": {
            "name": "...",
            "tokenLimit": 100000
          },
          "scraperAllowance": {
            "remaining": 97500
          }
        }
      },
      "headers": {}
    }

Report the fields the user asked about. The response also carries account
identity and billing identifiers; do not repeat them unless the user asks.
Check remaining tokens before a large batch of page retrievals. status reports
account usage, not the progress of a request.

## Step 6 — Troubleshoot

- Missing tools: enable or reconnect the MrScraper MCP connection, then confirm
  all seven tools are exposed.
- Unauthorized or expired authorization: reauthorize the OAuth 2.1 connection
  through the MCP client.
- 403 insufficient_scope: reauthorize so the client requests scrape:read for
  scraping and search, or account:read for status.
- Input-contract error: inspect the tool schema and omit inputs that do not
  apply. scraperAPI was replaced by scrapeHtml, scrapeMarkdown, and
  getScreenshot; brand and JSON extraction are scrapeBrand and scrapeJson; and
  webSearch takes query, country, and numResults.
- Page incomplete or missing dynamic content: load mrscraper-fetch and revise
  page-loading inputs deliberately.
- Search results weak: load mrscraper-serp and refine the query, country, or
  number of results.

## Limits

Use another tool for:

- Clicking controls, completing forms, or authenticated browser sessions.
- Parsing local PDFs, documents, spreadsheets, or other files.
- Recurring monitoring, notifications, or scheduling.

Explain the boundary and continue with any supported portion of the task.

# MrScraper for OpenCode

MrScraper connects [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) to a hosted MCP server for
retrieving public web pages as HTML, Markdown, or screenshots, web
search, and account usage. The plugin also includes three focused skills
that help OpenCode choose the right workflow and preserve raw page content.

The same package works in OpenCode 2 and OpenCode 1.

## What this plugin adds

- An MCP server named `mrscraper` that points at the hosted Streamable HTTP
  endpoint `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp`.
- OAuth 2.1 sign-in handled by OpenCode; no credential is stored in this
  package.
- The `mrscraper`, `mrscraper-fetch`, and `mrscraper-serp` skills.
- A retrieve-first workflow that keeps raw page responses available for
  analysis, verification, and follow-up transformations.

If your configuration already defines a `mrscraper` MCP server, the plugin
keeps your entry and only adds the skills. It also leaves any skill with the
same name that you already have in place.

## Requirements

- OpenCode 2 (verified with 2.0.26), or OpenCode 1.18.29 or later (verified
  with 1.18.29 and 1.19.0). On older OpenCode 1 releases, pin
  `@mrscraper/opencode@0.1.0`.
- A [MrScraper](https://app.mrscraper.com) account.
- Permission to access and process the target content.

## Install

### OpenCode 2

```bash
opencode plugin add @mrscraper/opencode
```

This adds the package to `plugins` in your global configuration. To enable it
for one project instead, add it to that project's `opencode.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@mrscraper/opencode"]
}
```

### OpenCode 1

```bash
opencode plugin @mrscraper/opencode --global
```

Or add the package to the `plugin` list in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`
(all projects) or a project's `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["@mrscraper/opencode"]
}
```

OpenCode installs npm plugins when it starts and caches them.

## Sign in

```bash
opencode mcp auth mrscraper
```

In OpenCode 2 you can also run `/mcps` in a session, select `mrscraper`, and
sign in there. OpenCode opens the MrScraper consent page in your browser,
registers its own OAuth client, and stores the tokens outside your project
configuration. Never paste OAuth tokens or API keys into chat.

Check the connection:

```bash
opencode mcp list
```

`mrscraper` shows `needs authentication` before sign-in and `connected`
afterwards.

On a machine without a local browser, use an API key instead (next section).
OpenCode 1 waits for the browser on `http://127.0.0.1:19876/mcp/oauth/callback`,
so you can also forward that port, for example
`ssh -L 19876:127.0.0.1:19876 <host>`.

## Use an API key instead of OAuth

Create a key at [app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens](https://app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens),
export it as `MRSCRAPER_API_KEY` in the environment that starts OpenCode, and
define the server yourself.

OpenCode 2 (`opencode.jsonc`):

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@mrscraper/opencode"],
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "mrscraper": {
        "type": "remote",
        "url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp",
        "oauth": false,
        "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {env:MRSCRAPER_API_KEY}" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

OpenCode 1 (`opencode.json`):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["@mrscraper/opencode"],
  "mcp": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp",
      "oauth": false,
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer {env:MRSCRAPER_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

OpenCode substitutes `{env:MRSCRAPER_API_KEY}` when it loads the configuration,
so the key stays out of the file. In OpenCode 2 the substitution happens in the
background service, so the variable must be set where the service starts; after
setting it, run `opencode service restart` from that shell. An API key carries
your full account authority; OAuth scopes do not apply to it.

## Try it

```text
Fetch https://www.scrapethissite.com and summarize the page.
```

The server provides these tools. OpenCode 1 shows them as `mrscraper_<tool>`;
OpenCode 2 reaches MCP tools through Code Mode by default.

| Tool | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | Return the raw account status API response without summarizing, redacting body fields, or adding calculated fields. |
| `scrapeHtml` | Retrieve the raw HTML of a page. Browser rendering is optional. |
| `scrapeMarkdown` | Retrieve a page as Markdown. Including HTML also enables browser rendering and returns both outputs as JSON. |
| `getScreenshot` | Capture a base64 screenshot of the full page or top viewport. Browser rendering is always enabled. |
| `scrapeBrand` | Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links as JSON. |
| `scrapeJson` | Extract structured JSON from a page using a natural-language prompt. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. |
| `webSearch` | Search the web and return ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources. |

## Retrieve-first routing

When a public URL is already known, the skills direct OpenCode to retrieve it
with `scrapeMarkdown` or `scrapeHtml` first and treat the raw response as the
source of truth. The agent can read, summarize, compare, or derive structured
output locally without losing details.

For roughly 100 known pages with a shared layout, the agent can retrieve pages
concurrently, retain every raw response, and apply one reusable local
extractor.

## Data and permissions

The plugin sends MCP tool inputs, including target URLs and search queries, to
MrScraper's hosted service. Page responses and tool results are then available
to OpenCode and its model provider for the requested task. Use it only with
public or otherwise authorized content, and follow the target site's
requirements.

Review MrScraper's [MCP documentation](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server),
[Privacy Policy](https://mrscraper.com/privacy-policy),
[Acceptable Use Policy](https://mrscraper.com/acceptable-use-policy), and
[Terms of Use](https://mrscraper.com/terms-of-use) before use.

## Update or remove

OpenCode 2 checks unpinned npm plugins for updates without installing them.
Update or remove the plugin with:

```bash
opencode plugin update @mrscraper/opencode
opencode plugin remove @mrscraper/opencode
```

In OpenCode 1, an unpinned entry stays on the version OpenCode first cached.
To control updates, pin a version and change it when you upgrade:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["@mrscraper/opencode@0.5.0"]
}
```

To remove it from OpenCode 1, delete the entry from `plugin`. In either
version, remove the stored OAuth tokens afterwards:

```bash
opencode mcp logout mrscraper
```

You can also revoke access under Connected applications in your MrScraper
account.

## Support and security

- Product help: [MrScraper MCP documentation](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server)
- Bugs and feature requests: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/mrscraper-com/mrscraper-opencode-plugin/issues)
- Account help: [support@mrscraper.com](mailto:support@mrscraper.com)
- Security reports: see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)

## Development

```text
index.ts        default export with an OpenCode 2 `setup()` and an OpenCode 1
                `server()`; both register the MCP server and the skills
skills/         MCP-oriented skills, copied verbatim from
                mrscraper-com/mrscraper-claude-plugin (plugins/mrscraper/skills)
```

```bash
npm install
npm run check
npm pack --dry-run
```

Test a local checkout in both majors before a release. In OpenCode 2, add the
checkout's absolute path to `plugins`, then run `opencode mcp list` and
`opencode api skill.list`. In OpenCode 1, add it to `plugin`, then run
`opencode mcp list` and `opencode debug skill`. Record user-visible changes in

# Changelog

All notable changes to the MrScraper OpenCode plugin are documented here. The
project follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## 0.5.0 - 2026-11-20

- Updated the skills, README, and publishing checklist for MrScraper MCP
  server 0.5.0, which follows the MrScraper Integrations Standard. The server
  has seven tools with the standard descriptions: `status`, `scrapeHtml`,
  `scrapeMarkdown`, `getScreenshot`, `scrapeBrand`, `scrapeJson`, and
  `webSearch`. `scraperAPI` is gone; use `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`, or
  `getScreenshot`, and `scrapeBrand` or `scrapeJson` for brand data and JSON
  extraction. `webSearch` now takes `query`, `country`, and `numResults`
  instead of `url`, `region`, `num_results`, and `timeout`, and all tool
  inputs are camelCase. Skills are identical to the MrScraper Claude 0.4.0,
  Cursor 0.5.0, Grok 0.4.0, and Antigravity 0.4.0 plugins.
- The hosted server now uses two OAuth scopes: `scrape:read` for the six
  scraping and search tools and `account:read` for `status`. Connections that
  already hold `scrape:read` keep working; `scrape:write` is no longer needed.

## 0.4.0 - 2026-11-02

- Updated the `mrscraper-serp` skill for MrScraper MCP server 0.3.0, which
  moved `webSearch` to MrScraper's new web search endpoint. Results are a
  ranked list (rank, title, url, description, source); `region` sets the
  results' country and the new `num_results` asks for 10 to 100 results. The
  `raw`, `format`, `language`, `page`, and `render_js` options are gone, and
  so is the search results URL example. Skills are identical to the MrScraper
  Claude plugin 0.3.0.

## 0.3.2 - 2026-10-29

- Reworded search as web search in the package
  description, keywords, README, and skills.
  The `webSearch` tool is unchanged. The skills now differ from the MrScraper
  Claude plugin 0.2.2 only in this wording.

## 0.3.1 - 2026-10-22

- Updated the `mrscraper` skill for the hosted server's three scopes:
  `scraperAPI` needs `scrape:write`, `webSearch` needs `scrape:read`, and
  `status` needs `account:read`. If `scraperAPI` returns 403
  `insufficient_scope`, run `opencode mcp auth mrscraper` again so OpenCode
  requests `scrape:write`. Skills are identical to the MrScraper Claude plugin
  0.2.2.

## 0.3.0 - 2026-10-14

- Updated the skills for the hosted MCP server's new tools: `scraperAPI`
  (pages as HTML, Markdown, or screenshots), `webSearch` (Google), and `status`
  (account usage). The `fetch`, `scrape`, `serp`, `rerun`, `results`, and
  `result` tools no longer exist.
- Removed the `mrscraper-scrape` skill. Skills are identical to the MrScraper
  Claude plugin 0.2.0.

## 0.2.0 - 2026-10-12

- Added OpenCode 2 support. OpenCode 2 does not run OpenCode 1 plugins; the
  package now default-exports one object with an OpenCode 2 `setup()`, which
  registers the `mrscraper` MCP server and the four skills through MCP and
  skill transforms, and an OpenCode 1 `server()`, which keeps the existing
  config hook.
- OpenCode 1 now needs 1.18.29 or later (the first release that loads the
  object form). On older releases, pin `@mrscraper/opencode@0.1.0`.
- The `MrScraperPlugin` named export was removed; use the default export.
- Documented OpenCode 2 install, sign-in, API-key configuration
  (`mcp.servers`), and update commands.

## 0.1.0 - 2026-10-05

- Added the initial `@mrscraper/opencode` plugin: registers the hosted
  MrScraper MCP server (`https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp`, OAuth 2.1) as
  `mrscraper` unless the user already defines that server, and loads the
  `mrscraper`, `mrscraper-fetch`, `mrscraper-scrape`, and `mrscraper-serp`
  skills from the MrScraper Claude plugin 0.1.4.
